initialAdequacy.rationale: Twelve substantive inspected works now include Texas and Louisiana community histories, an Oklahoma community perspective, a community-coauthored language-project chapter, a community constitution, federal statutes, an edited treaty transcription and older scholarship. Together they support a bounded educational introduction on distinct communities, language work and Texas legal history. The count is a quantity measure, not a claim that the collection is complete, exhaustive, endorsed by all communities, or suitable for current legal advice.
remainingLimits: The Texas statute’s contemplated proclamation and its implementation record were not inspected.
The treaty is an edited transcription; manuscript, ratification record and Indigenous responses remain unexamined.
The 1932 secondary article uses older terminology; more Coushatta-authored history and archival evidence would deepen the record.
Direct Koasati learning materials and current language/community context remain open.
No community review or endorsement has been recorded.
